concurrent-tools: The TS started the four tools' installs together (Promise.all over installOrUpdateTool), so the order of their log lines and of their requests across tools followed the promise scheduler: the three feed lookups, then the three HEADs, then the three archive GETs, with a failed download's warning landing after the other tools' 'Downloaded' lines. The Rust get_latest does the tools one after the other in the same list order (vkd3d, dxvk, dxvk-nvapi, dxvk-macOS), so each tool's lookup, download, extraction and version file complete before the next starts. Every line and every request is the golden's; the golden_dxvk.rs comparison groups the lines of that block by tool (each tool's own order kept) and compares the requests as a sorted set. The first run of a fresh install downloads three archives one after another instead of at once.
feed-failure-is-not-fatal-to-the-others: A failed feed lookup rejected the whole TS getLatest while the other tools' installs kept running unawaited. The Rust get_latest tries every tool and returns the first failure once all were tried, so the result is the same rejection and the other tools are still brought up to date. No golden carries a failing feed.
missing-latest-is-an-error-value: When getLatest installed nothing (offline, or the download failed), the TS read latest_<tool> anyway and the readFileSync threw ENOENT, which rejected installRemove (87-09 findings 1; the offline and download-failure goldens' 'thrown'). The Rust install_remove returns Err(DxvkError::MissingLatest) in those cases, and the op answers 'wine_dxvk_install_remove:missing-latest'. The golden pins that it is a rejection; Node's error text, which names the file, is not reproduced.
copies-finish-before-the-call-returns: The source-less install started its DLL copies and the current_<tool> write without awaiting them, so installRemove resolved before they landed (87-09 finding 2; the oracle waited for the tree to settle). The Rust copies and the version write are done before install_remove returns, so the tree is the golden's with no wait. A copy that fails is logged and the install goes on, as in the TS.
dll-names-are-sorted: readdirSync listed the tool directories in the file system's order, which decided the order of the reg add and reg delete commands. The Rust install_remove reads the names sorted, which is the order the goldens recorded (APFS lists by name) and is the same on every file system.
error-text: A log line that ends in an error object (Error removing <path>, Error when downloading <tool>, Error when copying <dll>) carried Node's error message in the TS: 'Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat ...' or the AxiosError text. The Rust line ends in the OS error text or the fetch error's category word ('status(500)'), which names no URL (T-87-09). The golden_dxvk.rs comparison keeps the subject of each such line (its first three or four words) and ignores what follows.
log-prefix: Every golden log line carries the TS prefix ToolInstaller. The engine log is a level and one line and has no prefix field, so the Rust lines carry none; the test asserts every golden line is ToolInstaller and compares the level and the message.
dialog-keys: The backend jest project stubs i18next to return the key, so the download-failure showDialog golden carries box.error.dxvk.title and box.error.dxvk.message (87-09 finding 6). The Rust run resolves them through the catalog; the test loads the English catalog and compares the resolved text to the English of the golden's keys. The dialog has no acknowledgement id (the TS passed null).
replaced-version-removed: The TS left every earlier version of a tool under <tools>/<tool> forever. The Rust install_or_update_tool removes the version a successful update replaces, and the archive, through gamelib-safety with <tools>/<tool> as the trust root (D-17); a version named by latest_<tool> that is not one plain folder name is not removed. No golden updates a tool that was already installed over a download, so no golden tree differs.
archive-with-no-repack-asset: For the macOS DXVK a feed whose first asset is the -builtin one and that has no repack.tar.gz made the TS dereference undefined and throw a TypeError. The Rust pick_asset answers a bad-feed error. No golden carries it.
extract-failure-cleans-up: A failed extraction left the half-made directory under <tools>/<tool>/<version> in the TS (and wrote no version file). The Rust install_or_update_tool removes that directory through gamelib-safety too, so a symlink a hostile archive made is never left behind. No golden carries a failing tar.
log-lines-carry-the-prefix-path: The evidence lines the live gates cite ('installing <tool> on... <prefix>') and the 'Error removing <path>' lines name the prefix, as in the TS, because the goldens and the gates pin them. They are the only log lines of this module that carry a profile path; the feed and download lines carry no URL.
